cohorts.summary: Asymmetrical multiplayer action and voice chat create chaotic matches despite complex maps.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that proximity voice chat is a central feature that creates funny and chaotic multiplayer moments while being chased by SCPs.

citations.review_text: proximity chat + scp = horror game with more than enough laughter

SCP: Secret Laboratory is a free-to-play multiplayer horror game based on the SCP Foundation universe. It combines survival horror, role-playing, teamwork, and chaotic multiplayer encounters as players take on different roles inside a facility during a containment breach.

The biggest strength of SCP: Secret Laboratory is its unpredictable gameplay. Every match can play out completely differently depending on the roles players receive and the decisions they make. One game might involve escaping as a Class-D subject, while another could have you working as security, controlling dangerous SCPs, or trying to restore order.

The role system is the game's greatest feature. Each team has different objectives, abilities, and challenges, creating a constantly changing experience. SCPs must hunt and contain players, humans must survive and escape, and other factions may have their own hidden goals.

The atmosphere is another major highlight. The dark facility setting, creepy SCP creatures, alarms, and tense moments create a strong horror feeling. The game successfully captures the fear and uncertainty of being trapped in a dangerous research facility.

The multiplayer community also adds a lot of entertainment. Voice chat creates hilarious, dramatic, and unexpected moments, especially when players cooperate, betray each other, or create their own stories during matches.

However, the biggest weakness is that the experience depends heavily on the players. A good group can create unforgettable matches, but uncooperative players, trolling, or poor teamwork can sometimes ruin the atmosphere.

The learning curve can also be difficult for new players. There are many roles, SCP behaviours, items, and mechanics to understand, and the game does not always explain everything clearly. New players may need several matches before they fully understand what is happening.

Replay value is one of SCP: Secret Laboratory's strongest points. The variety of roles, random events, updates, and pl…
Super fun, the prox chat makes getting chased hilarious. I honestly have no complaints

SCP: Secret Laboratory is one of those games where every match feels like a fever dream.

I love how unpredictable it is. One game you’re trying to survive as a Class-D, the next you’re a scientist, security, or an SCP causing absolute chaos. You never know what’s going to happen, and that’s what makes every round so fun.

The SCP universe is already something I’m a huge fan of, so getting to experience a Site-02 containment breach with other players is amazing. The teamwork, betrayals, random friendships, and hilarious moments make every match memorable.

Also, PINK CANDY BOOM (candy cult) are some of the funniest chaos this game has to offer. Nothing says "everything is under control" like someone pulling out a suspicious piece of candy and turning the entire situation into a disaster.

The voice chat creates some of the best moments too. One second everyone is making a serious plan, and the next everything has completely fallen apart.

Containment breach, terrible decisions, and pink candy explosions. What more could you want?

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the map layout as difficult to navigate, causing players to get lost.

citations.review_text: SCP: Secret Laboratory is one of the most difficult and terrifying multiplayer games I’ve played. Every round feels unpredictable, and the constant threat of SCPs makes even simple objectives incredibly stressful. The difficulty comes from having to learn the maps, understand different roles, manage resources, and work with teammates while everything is falling apart. The SCPs themselves are genuinely scary, especially when you hear footsteps or realize something is hunting you in the dark. Even when you know what’s coming, the game can still make you panic. It’s frustrating at times, but that challenge makes surviving feel incredibly rewarding.The atmosphere makes the difficulty even worse, with dark hallways, limited information, and sudden encounters keeping you constantly nervous. You never truly feel safe, even when you’re with other players. Every escape feels earned, and every mistake can quickly turn into a terrifying chase or a brutal death.
Good game only problem i get lost in the map 90% of the time i can only follow poeple to figure out where is what but its a good game none the last

this game is good but i dont know how can i have good fps

If I'm being honest, one of, if not the worst game I have ever played. I will summarize all the points that i don't like about the game.
 
First of all: The game is heavily luck-based. Every round, the map is changed, making it so you cannot improve at map learning/awareness. This makes dealing with SCP-173 a headache, as a dead end can be reached. Not only are the maps random, but also the gunfight, wich will be my next point.

Second of all: It has one of the worst gunfights I've ever get to experience in a game. You can't get better at aiming, because, again, it's a system based on pure luck.

Third of all: The movement on this game makes no sense, as well as it being cluncky and very buggy. You tell me that humans can jump with <20lb gear, but can't crouch???? Also it just simply looks stupid, and boring.

FOURTH of all: The performance... Even with my specs, it isn't enough (Not getting more than 120 fps on low settings, as well as in normal servers). Garten of Banban was something, but this...

Fifth of all: The SCP experience (Killer gameplay) can sometimes be frustrating. This by itself isn't something wrong, but when you realize that, if no human opens the gate and doesn't activate Warhead, killers just simply cannot play. Moreover, when playing on a full lobby, if killers play together (this applies mostly to SCP-096), they can't be killed. Simple as that. I want to point out something that, retroBreach, an SCP Multiplayer Roblox Game does better than this one. When SCP-096 rages, he can kill everyone, whether you saw him or not, BUT, when his rage ends, there is a 30 second timer until he can rage again. (It's called balancing).

To conclude, if you like SCP, I wouldn't recommend this game. No way. In general, every multiplayer SCP game, sadly, feels that way. The ONLY good thing this game has, is voice chat. The ONLY feature. And don't be surprised if you encounter people feeling like gods at the game. "Buddy, this game has no skill gap, it's pure luck."…
